messages.author: 373e56ec89625c50
messages.subject: user-supplied polychoric correlation matrix?
parts:
is it possible to manually supply lavaan with a polychoric correlation matrix obtained somewhere else? i'm working on a different (Bayesian) estimation of it but I have never seen any uses for the polychoric correlation matrix aside of an 'intermediate' step (à la PRELIS/LISREL) to fit SEM models with categorical data and I would like to take advantage of the lavaan structure to obtain parameter estimates without having to code everything from scratch myself.

thank you!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: user-supplied polychoric correlation matrix?
parts:
On 04/20/2014 06:08 AM, Oscar Olvera wrote:
> is it possible to manually supply lavaan with a polychoric correlation
> matrix obtained somewhere else?

> estimation of it but I have never seen any uses for the polychoric
> correlation matrix aside of an 'intermediate' step (à la PRELIS/LISREL)
> to fit SEM models with categorical data and I would like to take
> advantage of the lavaan structure to obtain parameter estimates without
> having to code everything from scratch myself.

I'm not sure what you want/need. You can supply any matrix to the
sample.cov= argument, and perhaps use do.fit=FALSE, if you only want to
setup the internals of a lavaan object, without actually estimating any
parameters.

Of course, if you need more control, you can call any internal lavaan
function using lavaan:::someFunction() in your own script. If you want
to know what a particular (internal) function is doing, let me know.

Yves.

Sorry for not being clear. I may be wrong on this one (although I am almost certain I am not) but when one fits a SEM model to ordered categorical data, using only the matrix of polychoric correlations is not enough. The full data set is required so that the proper weight matrix W can also be computed and whatnot. I know that I use lavaan to fit a model to discrete data, the internal lavaan engine will grab the data, calculate the polychoric correlation matrix, the W matrix and and use some algorithm from the family of weighted-least squares to get me parameter estimates. What I was wondering is that if in these steps of (1) take the data (2) calculate polychoric correlations (3) calculate the W matrix  (4) use weighted least squares  i could substitute step #2 by giving lavaan my own, external polychoric correlation matrix instead of the one calculated by default.

Kind of like how it used to be in the old LISREL where the polychoric correlation matrix had to be calculated separately (I think on PRELIS?), saved in a datafile and then fed back so that LISREL could do all the necessary calculations.

Thanks! (and sorry for the late reply!)
